answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards, choose players+1 face-down onto the board, and return the rest unseen. Put encounter tokens on the 11 marked territories; randomly choose a face-up structure bonus tile below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

At setup, put the character at home; two workers on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining home; four mechs over Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in black-square green boxes; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits in bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; and the action token ready beside the Player Mat. Leave Faction Mat one-time recruit spaces empty. The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; the Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards.

Yes: after moving to a different section from last turn, you may take neither action. Rusviet may repeat a section (including its Factory card); top and bottom are each still limited to once that turn. Top-row gains can pay the bottom-row cost. If taking both, top must precede bottom. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before choosing as much or as little of exposed green-box benefits as desired; exact costs/benefits are on the Player Mat and may change with upgrades.

An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls that territory and its resources. The enemy does not gain your structure’s abilities; you keep those abilities, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Spend resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.

No: normal Move selects up to two different units, one adjacent territory each, and cannot move the same unit twice. A transported worker’s carried movement does not count as its own, so it may later move itself. All units can carry any number of resources; only mechs can also carry any number of your workers, never your character.

The mech may enter, then stops and cannot move again that turn; enemy workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources. You lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; having zero popularity does not prevent retreat. Your workers cannot independently enter while enemy workers control the territory.
answers.evidence: Actions — Move OR coins, “Enemy workers only”

answers.answer: After all units finish a Move action, resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. Your workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.

Bolster costs $1 and gives two power OR one combat card (before upgrades). If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) OR one popularity (before upgrades). Put traded resources on a controlled territory containing at least one worker; if all workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources. Built Monument adds one popularity on Bolster; built Armory adds one power on Trade.

Pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline any or all production, including workers. Newly exposed costs apply to future Produce actions, not the one already paid.

Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes; move a cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost (solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded). Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; put a chosen mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake, and its uncovered ability then applies to your character and every mech, not workers. Costs vary by mat/upgrades. Even after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits, you may pay a bottom action to get its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.

Build on a controlled territory with your worker; one structure total per territory, including opponents’ structures; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A controlled Mill adds one Produce territory; it cannot produce when uncontrolled. Your Mine remains your personal tunnel for your units’ movement even when enemy-controlled; opponents cannot use your building abilities.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions — Build; Control, resources and home bases

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row Player Mat section and place it permanently on any open one-time bonus space on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain the chosen one-time bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed. When you, your immediate left, or immediate right neighbor takes that corresponding bottom action, resolve active player first, then left, then right; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play the opponent triggers once, not twice.

Both combatants secretly and simultaneously choose dial power from 0 to the smaller of seven and current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech; Rusviet People’s Army adds one card if any workers are present. If both have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and total dial plus card values; attacker wins ties. Both deduct selected dial power from their Power Tracks and discard every played card face-up; card values do not deduct track power.

Loser’s characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their home base (Nordic Seaworthy units/carried workers may instead retreat to an adjacent lake), leaving all resources on the battle territory. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none, subject to Polania Camaraderie. A non-Saxony winner places a combat star only if they have zero or one combat stars; with two, none. Saxony places one after each victory while star tokens remain. A loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.

After the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains on the encounter territory, discard its token and draw a card before a following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. All gained resources, workers, mechs, and structures go on the encounter territory. Pay the card’s printed cost, but no normal action costs or mat benefits/ongoing recruit bonuses apply.

Each player’s character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning any combat), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot take or exchange one. It is a fifth action section, optional top then bottom under usual no-repeat rules (Rusviet exception); similar actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories in that Move action, or three for a Speed-enabled character/mech; Mine access and normal movement/stop rules apply.

Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; you may wait, but must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Put a star on the Triumph Track objective space and return the completed card to the objective deck bottom. Normally return the other objective card there too. Saxony may complete both starting objectives and keeps the other card after completing the first, for up to two objective stars.

Stars are earned for six upgrades; four deployed mechs; four built structures; four recruits; all eight workers on the board; one revealed completed objective; combat victories (up to two stars, with Saxony’s exception); 18 popularity; or 16 power. A star is permanent even if power/popularity later drops; another player’s star does not block the goal. The sixth star ends play immediately, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — Stars and immediate end

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. Resolve a neighbor’s power/popularity recruit star after the active action, in order active player, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for game end each time; after a sixth star, no later recruit star/bonus resolves. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that movement portion, returning initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — Stars and immediate end

answers.answer: At popularity 10, the 7–12 tier gives $4 per star, $3 per territory counted, and $2 per complete pair of controlled resources. Thus 5 stars add $20; four normal territories plus the Factory count as 7 and add $21; 13 resources make 6 pairs and add $12; these categories add $53 to held coins, plus the selected structure bonus. Structures qualify for that bonus even when enemies control their territories. Victory tiebreakers: workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, then stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune; Structure bonus eligibility; Most total coins wins

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move back into any home base, build there, or deploy there; setup, forced retreats, and Crimea’s unlocked Wayfare are exceptions. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.

Mountain produces metal, tundra oil, farm food, forest wood, village a worker; lake and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Actions — Produce; Control, resources and home bases

answers.answer: Any unit may pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources mid-movement; only mechs may also carry your workers, and mechs may never carry your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one step and the extra Speed step may be before or after it. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
Yes. Any unit entering a territory with only an enemy structure takes control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Actions — Move OR coins, “Enemy structure only”; printed tunnel territories

answers.answer: You may take a legal dead turn: move the action token to a different section and take neither action. You never pay only part of a cost.

Armory grants one power on Trade; Monument grants one popularity on Bolster. These are benefits on those matching top actions. You retain your structure abilities even without control, except the Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory; enemy units do not gain your structure’s abilities.
answers.evidence: Actions — Bolster; Trade; Control, resources and home bases

answers.answer: Riverwalk is an unlockable mech ability for each faction and applies to character and all mechs, not workers: Nordic and Saxony cross rivers into forests/mountains; Rusviet into farms/villages; Crimea into farms/tundra; Polania into villages/mountains. Nordic Swim is its separate starting ability: workers alone may cross rivers to land terrain, not lakes; it does not apply to Nordic character/mechs.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities — Riverwalk

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities — Saxony Underpass; Rusviet Township

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine: opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery instead lets you pay one power to reduce opponent’s power by two before combat, once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities — Saxony; Nordic

answers.answer: Two mechs and three workers permit three cards total: one per participating character/mech plus one extra from People’s Army when any workers are present. Workers alone never fight; a character or mech must participate.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities — Rusviet Township; Special Rules — Combat

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to your own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. They cannot enter an active opponent’s home base.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities — Crimea Wayfare

answers.answer: Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Crimea Coercion lets you spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of its value.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities — Crimea; Crimea starting ability

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake; it gives no Nordic-style adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes need a mech to move off, and you cannot leave carried workers or resources behind on a lake when their carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities — Nordic Seaworthy; Polania Submerge

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not protect against popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities — Polania Camaraderie

answers.answer: Polania Meander may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; the first gain can pay the second option’s cost. The summary does not give a different encounter-card count: its encounter procedure says draw a card.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities — Polania Meander; Encounters

answers.answer: No: a character entering an encounter token territory stops and cannot move again that turn. Resolve the encounter after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there; this applies to Factory Move too.

Combat-card hand count is public, but contents stay secret until revealed; during combat you may conceal whether you committed any cards until reveal. Objective contents are secret until a completed objective is revealed. Coins are not hidden information, but you need not reveal their total value when asked.

Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable; agreements are informal and unenforceable. (In tournament play, even coin exchanges for deals/alliances are forbidden.) A payment cannot cancel combat already initiated by moving plastic units onto opposing units; combat occurs after Move, though bribes may influence its outcome.

Popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per territory counted, $1 per pair of controlled resources. Popularity 7–12: $4, $3, $2 respectively. Popularity 13–18: $5, $4, $3 respectively. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Only complete resource pairs score; a single leftover resource is ignored.

For adjacency bonuses, count each unique feature once across all structures; rivers do not break adjacency. Encounter locations count even after their tokens are removed. Tunnel tiles count printed tunnels, not Mines. The summary provides these payouts: adjacent tunnels: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6=$9; adjacent encounters: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9; adjacent lakes: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9.

Structures on tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Structures in a row scores only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Structures on farms/tundras counts combined qualifying structures: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including a worker carried by a defeated mech on a lake. Polania Camaraderie may provide its stated exception.
No. The star stays placed permanently, but current popularity determines final scoring. Other players’ stars never block a goal, so two factions can each earn a star for the same achievement.

Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Sit near your faction home base; clockwise from the board top, faction seating order is Nordic → Rusviet → Crimea → Saxony → Polania, omitting inactive factions. The summary states recruit bonuses trigger for immediate left/right neighbors, but does not state why the seating arrangement matters beyond identifying those neighbors.

A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability can enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
No. Show the encounter card to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.
There is no limit on friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.
No. Top and bottom actions are each limited to once within the turn, including for Rusviet. Rusviet may repeat a section, which waives only the previous-turn section restriction.
You may take the alternative Move benefit and gain $1.
No. Workers never return to the Player Mat.
Yes. You may attack with zero power and/or zero popularity.
Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; a non-Saxony winner with two combat stars simply places no further combat star.

A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option; it cannot decline to choose any option. It cannot select unaffordable coin/popularity options. It may take as little of the chosen benefit as desired.
No turn order: both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose their dials (and cards), then reveal simultaneously.
Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.

A star is placed as soon as its goal is achieved; you cannot decline or delay it. A completed objective is the exception: you may wait to reveal it, but must satisfy all requirements at the moment you reveal it.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end; Objectives and agreements

answers.answer: No. By default units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes; faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.
No. The recruit is placed permanently on the chosen one-time bonus space and cannot later move.
No. Only a character triggers an encounter; entering with a mech or worker does not trigger or remove the token.

A controlled Mill adds one bonus territory to the current Produce allowance: two normal territories become up to three, or an upgraded allowance of three becomes up to four. The Mill itself counts as one producing worker and can produce without an actual worker there, using the terrain table; actual workers there also produce normally, so Mill output is added to theirs. It only works while controlled.
answers.evidence: Actions — Produce; Control, resources and home bases

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish or preserve control; leaving the last unit without a structure means you no longer control it.
Build costs wood; Enlist costs food.
